translations.text: The record of the ancestry of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham.
Abraham fathered Isaac, Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob fathered Judah and his brothers.
Judah fathered Perez and Zerah by Tamar. Perez fathered Hezron, and Hezron fathered Aram.
Aram fathered Amminadab, Amminadab fathered Nahshon, and Nahshon fathered Salmon.
Salmon fathered Boaz by Rahab. Boaz fathered Obed by Ruth, and Obed fathered Jesse.
Jesse fathered King David, and David fathered Solomon by Uriah’s wife.
Solomon fathered Rehoboam, Rehoboam fathered Abijah, and Abijah fathered Asaph.
Asaph fathered Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat fathered Joram, and Joram fathered Uzziah.
Uzziah fathered Jotham, Jotham fathered Ahaz, and Ahaz fathered Hezekiah.
Hezekiah fathered Manasseh, Manasseh fathered Amos, and Amos fathered Josiah.
Josiah fathered Jeconiah and his brothers at the time of the deportation to Babylon.
After the deportation to Babylon, Jeconiah fathered Shealtiel, and Shealtiel fathered Zerubbabel.
Zerubbabel fathered Abiud, Abiud fathered Eliakim, and Eliakim fathered Azor.
Azor fathered Zadok, Zadok fathered Achim, and Achim fathered Eliud.
Eliud fathered Eleazar, Eleazar fathered Matthan, and Matthan fathered Jacob.
Jacob fathered Joseph, the husband of Mary, from whom Jesus was born, who is called Christ.

So all the generations from Abraham to David were fourteen generations, from David to the deportation to Babylon fourteen generations, and from the deportation to Babylon to Christ fourteen generations.
The birth of Jesus Christ happened this way: when his mother Mary was engaged to Joseph, before they came together, she was found to be pregnant through the Holy Spirit.
Joseph, her husband, was a righteous man and did not want to expose her publicly, so he wanted to divorce her secretly.

While he was thinking about these things, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in a dream, saying, "Joseph, son of David, do not be afraid to take Mary as your wife, for the child who will be born from her is from the Holy Spirit."
"She will give birth to a son, and you are to name him Jesus, for he is the one who will save his people from their sins."
All this happened so that what the Lord had spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled, saying:
"Look, the virgin will conceive and give birth to a son, and they will name him Emmanuel," which is translated, "God is with us."
Joseph woke from sleep and did as the angel of the Lord had commanded him. He took Mary as his wife.
He did not have sexual relations with her until she gave birth to her son, and he named him Jesus.
After Jesus was born in Bethlehem in Judea, in the days of King Herod, magi came from the east to Jerusalem, saying:
"Where is the newborn king of the Jews? For we saw his star in the east and have come to worship him."
When King Herod heard this, he was greatly troubled, and all Jerusalem with him.
He gathered all the chief priests and the scribes of the people and asked them where the Christ would be born.
They told him, “In Bethlehem in Judea, for this is what is written through the prophet:
‘And you, Bethlehem, land of Judah, are by no means the least among the rulers of Judah, for a ruler will come from you who will shepherd my people Israel.’”
Then Herod secretly called the wise men and asked them about the time when the star had appeared.
He sent them to Bethlehem, saying, “Go and inquire carefully about the little child. When you find him, tell me too, so that I may come and worship him.”
After hearing the king, they went away. And look, the star they had seen in the east went ahead of them until it came and stood over the place where the little child was.
When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceedingly great joy.
When they entered the house, they saw the little child with Mary his mother. They fell down and worshiped him. They opened their treasures and brought him gifts: gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
They were warned in a dream not to return to Herod, so they went back to their country by another road.

After they had gone, look, the angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream, saying, “Get up, take the little child and his mother, and go to Egypt. Stay there until I tell you, for Herod will search for the little child to destroy him.”
He got up, took the little child and his mother during the night, and went to Egypt.
He stayed there until Herod died, so that what the Lord had said through the prophet would be fulfilled: “I called my son out of Egypt.”

Then Herod, when he saw that the wise men had mocked him, became extremely angry. He sent out and killed every little child in Bethlehem and throughout its surrounding districts, from two years old and under, according to the time determined by inquiry from the wise men.
Then what had been spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled:
“A voice was heard in Ramah, weeping and great mourning: Rachel weeping for her children. She would not be comforted, because they were not hers.”
After Herod died, look, the angel of the Lord appeared to Joseph in a dream in Egypt,
saying, “Get up, take the little child and his mother, and go to the land of Israel, for those who sought the little child’s life have died.”
He got up, took the little child and his mother, and went to the land of Israel.
But when he heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there. After being warned in a dream, he withdrew to the regions of Galilee.
He came and settled in a town called Nazareth, so that what was spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled: “He will be called a Nazarene.”
In those days John the Baptist came, preaching in the wilderness of Judea,
saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.”
For this is the one spoken of through Isaiah the prophet, who said, “The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.’”
John himself wore clothing made from camel hair, with a leather belt wrapped around his waist. His food was locusts and wild honey.
Then all Jerusalem, Judea, and the entire region around the Jordan were going out to him,
being baptized by him in the Jordan River and confessing their sins.
But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees coming for baptism, he said to them, “You offspring of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
So produce fruit worthy of repentance.
And do not think of saying to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones.
Even now the axe lies at the root of the trees. So every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
I baptize you with water for repentance, but the one who is coming is stronger than I am. I am not worthy to carry his sandals. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hand. He will clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into the storehouse, but he will burn the chaff with fire that cannot be put out.”
Then Jesus came from Galilee to the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him.
But he tried to stop him, saying, “I need to be baptized by you, and you are coming to me?”
But Jesus answered him, “Allow it for now, for this is how it is fitting for us to fulfill all righteousness.” Then he allowed him.
When Jesus had been baptized, he immediately came up out of the water. And look, the heavens opened, and he saw the Spirit of God coming down like a dove upon him.
And look, there was a voice from the heavens saying, “This is my Son, my beloved, in whom I am pleased.”
Then Jesus was led up into the wilderness by the Spirit to be tempted by the devil.
He fasted for forty days and forty nights, and afterward he was hungry.
The tempter approached him and said to him, “If you are the Son of God, command these stones to become bread.”
But he answered, “It is written: ‘A person will not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God.’”
Then the devil took him up into the holy city and made him stand on the pinnacle of the temple.

He said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here. For it is written: ‘He will give his angels orders concerning you, and they will lift you up on their hands, so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.’”
Jesus said again, “It is also written: ‘You must not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
Again the devil took him up onto a very high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory.
He said to him, “I will give you all these things if you fall down and worship me.”
Then Jesus said to him, “Go away, Satan! For it is written: ‘You must worship the Lord your God and serve him alone.’”
Then the devil left him, and look, angels came and served him.
When he heard that John had been handed over, he withdrew to Galilee.
He left Nazareth and came to live in Capernaum, which is beside the sea, in the territories of Zebulun and Naphtali.
This was so that what was spoken through the prophet Isaiah would be fulfilled, when he said:
“The land of Zebulun, the land of Naphtali, the road to the sea, the far side of the Jordan, Galilee of the Gentiles—
the people sitting in darkness have seen a great light, and for those living in the region and shadow of death, light has dawned.”
From that time on, Jesus began to preach, saying, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
As he was walking beside the Sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
He said to them, “Come, follow me, and I will make you fishers of people.”
They immediately left their nets and followed him.
Going a little farther, he saw two other brothers, James the son of Zebedee and John his brother, in the boat with Zebedee their father, mending their nets. He called them.
They immediately left their nets and their father and followed him.
He went throughout all Galilee, teaching in their synagogues, preaching the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every infirmity among the people.

His fame spread throughout all Syria. They brought him everyone who was suffering from various diseases and pains, those possessed by demons, those with epilepsy, and those who were paralyzed, and he healed them.
Large crowds followed him from Galilee, the Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and the other side of the Jordan.
When he saw the crowds, he went up the mountain. After he sat down, his disciples came to him.
He opened his mouth and taught them, saying:
“Blessed are the poor in spirit, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to them.
Blessed are those who mourn, for they will be comforted.
Blessed are the gentle, for they will inherit the earth.
Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they will be satisfied.
Blessed are the merciful, for they will be shown mercy.
Blessed are those who are pure in heart, for they will see God.
Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
Blessed are those who have been persecuted because of righteousness, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to them.
Blessed are you when people insult you, persecute you, and falsely say every kind of evil against you because of me.
Rejoice and be glad, for your reward in heaven is great. For this is how they persecuted the prophets who came before you.
You are the salt of the earth. But if the salt loses its taste, what will make it salty again? It is good for nothing except to be thrown out and trampled on by people.
You are the light of the world. A city situated on a mountain cannot be hidden.
Nor do people light a lamp and put it under a measuring basket. Instead, they put it on the lampstand, and it gives light to everyone in the house.
In the same way, let your light shine before people, so that they may see your good deeds and give glory to your Father in heaven.
Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them.
For truly I tell you, until heaven and earth pass away, not a single iota or a single stroke will disappear from the Law until everything has happened.

Therefore, whoever sets aside one of these least commandments and teaches people to do the same will be called least in the kingdom of heaven. But whoever practices them and teaches them will be called great in the kingdom of God.
For I tell you that unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
You have heard that it was said to the people of old, ‘You must not murder,’ and, ‘Whoever murders is liable to judgment.’

But I tell you that anyone who is angry with his brother without cause is liable to judgment. Whoever says to his brother, ‘You are worthless,’ is liable to the council. Whoever says, ‘You fool,’ is liable to fiery hell.
So if you come to offer your gift on the altar and remember there that your brother has something against you,
leave your gift there before the altar, and first go and make peace with your brother. Then come and offer your gift.

Come to an agreement quickly with the person bringing a lawsuit against you while you are with him on the way, lest your opponent hand you over to the judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and you are thrown into prison.
Truly I tell you, you will not come out of there until you have paid the last quadrans coin.
You have heard that it was said, “You must not commit adultery.”
But I tell you that anyone who looks at a woman with lust for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
If your right eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw it away from you. For it is better for you to lose one of your body parts than for your whole body to be thrown into fiery hell.
And if your right hand causes you to sin, cut it off and throw it away from you. For it is better for you to lose one of your body parts than for your whole body to be thrown into hell.
It was also said, ‘Whoever divorces his wife must give her a certificate of divorce.’

But I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on grounds of sexual immorality, causes adultery to be committed with her. And whoever marries a woman whose husband has divorced her is an adulterer.
Again, you have heard that it was said among the people of old, ‘You must not swear falsely, but you must fulfill your vows to the Lord.’
But I tell you, do not swear at all. Do not swear by heaven, because it is God's throne.
Nor swear by the earth, because it is the footstool for his feet. Nor swear by Jerusalem, because it is the city of the great King.
Nor swear by your head, because you cannot make a single hair white or black.
Let your words be ‘Yes, yes’ and ‘No, no.’ Anything beyond these comes from the evil one.
You have heard that it was said, ‘An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth.’
But I tell you, do not resist an evil person. Instead, if someone strikes you on your right cheek, turn the other one to him.
And if someone wants to sue you and take your tunic, let him have your cloak as well.
If someone forces you to go one mile, go two with him.
Give to the person who asks you, and do not turn away the person who wants to borrow from you.
You have heard that it was said, “Love your neighbor and hate your enemies.”
But I tell you: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
so that you may become children of your Father in heaven. For he makes his sun rise on the good and the evil, and he sends rain on the righteous and the unjust.
For if you love those who love you, what reward do you have? Do not the tax collectors themselves do the same?
And if you greet only your own people, what more are you doing? Do not the Gentiles themselves do this too?
So be perfect, just as your Father in heaven is perfect.
Be careful not to do your charitable giving in front of people so that they will see you. Otherwise, you have no reward with your Father in heaven.

So when you give to the needy, do not announce it loudly before you, as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets, so that people will honor them. Truly I tell you, they have already received their reward.
But when you give to the needy, do not let your left hand know what your right hand is doing.
So that your charitable giving may be done in secret, and your Father, who sees you in secret, will reward you.

And when you are about to pray, do not be like the hypocrites. They love to stand praying in the synagogues and at the street corners so that people will see them. Truly I tell you, they have already received their reward.
But when you are about to pray, go into your private room, shut your door, and pray to your Father who is in secret. And your Father, who sees you in secret, will reward you.
When you pray, do not use many words like the pagans, for they think they will be heard because of their many words.
So do not be like them, for God your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
This, then, is how you should pray: “Our Father in heaven, may your name be holy.
May your kingdom come. May your will be done on earth as it is in heaven.
Give us today our bread for the day to come.
Forgive us our debts, just as we too forgive those who owe us.
And do not lead us into temptation, but rescue us from the evil one. For yours are the power and the glory forever. Amen.”
For if you forgive people their sins, your Father in heaven will also forgive you your sins.
But if you do not forgive people their sins, your Father in heaven will not forgive you your sins.
When you fast, do not look gloomy like the hypocrites. They disfigure their faces so that people will see that they are fasting. Truly I tell you, they have already received their reward.
But when you fast, anoint your head and wash your face.
So that you do not appear to people to be fasting, but to your Father who is in secret; and your Father, who sees you in secret, will reward you.
Do not store up treasures for yourselves on earth, where moths and rust destroy, and where thieves break in and steal.
Instead, store up treasures for yourselves in heaven, where neither moths nor rust destroy, and where thieves do not break in and steal.
For where your treasure is, there your heart will be too.
The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body will be full of light.
But if your eye is evil, your whole body will be dark. So if the light within you is darkness, how great is that darkness!
No one can serve two masters. For either he will hate one and love the other, or he will cling to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.
That is why I tell you: Do not worry about your life, what you will eat or what you will drink, or about your body, what you will wear. Is not life more than food, and the body more than clothing?
Look at the birds of the sky: they neither sow nor reap nor gather into storehouses, yet your Father in heaven feeds them. Are you not worth much more than they are?
Which of you can add a cubit to his height by worrying?
And why do you worry about clothing? Look at the lilies of the field and how they grow: they neither labor nor spin.
I tell you that not even Solomon in all his glory was dressed like one of these.
If God clothes the grass of the field this way, though it is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the oven, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith!
So do not worry, saying, ‘What will we eat?’ or ‘What will we drink?’ or ‘What will we wear?’
For the Gentiles seek all these things, and your Father in heaven knows that you need them all.
But seek his kingdom and his righteousness first, and all these things will be added to you.
So do not worry about tomorrow, for tomorrow will worry about itself. Each day has enough trouble of its own.
Do not judge, so that you will not be judged.
For you will be judged by the judgment you give, and the measure you use will be used to measure for you.
Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but do not notice the beam in your own eye?
Or how can you say to your brother, ‘My brother, let me remove the speck from your eye,’ when there is a beam in your own eye?
You hypocrite! First remove the beam from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
Do not give holy things to dogs, and do not throw your pearls before pigs, lest they trample them with their feet and turn and tear you apart.
Ask, and you will be given; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks will receive, and whoever seeks will find, and the door will be opened for whoever knocks.
Or which person among you, if his son asks him for bread, will give him a stone?
Or if he asks him for a fish, will he give him a snake?
So if you, though you are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him!
So whatever you want people to do for you, do the same for them. For this is the Law and the Prophets.
Enter through the narrow gate, for the gate is wide and the road is broad that leads to destruction, and many will enter through it.
But the gate is narrow and the road is cramped that leads to life, and few will find it.
Beware of false prophets, who come to you in sheep’s clothing but inwardly are ravenous wolves.
You will recognize them by their fruit. Do people gather grapes from thorn bushes or pick figs from thistles?
This is how it is: every good tree produces good fruit, but a bad tree produces bad fruit.
A good tree cannot produce bad fruit, nor can a bad tree produce good fruit.
So every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
Therefore, you will recognize them by their fruit.
Not everyone who says to me, “Lord, Lord,” will enter the kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of my Father in heaven.
For many will say to me on that day, “Lord, Lord, did we not prophesy in your name and drive out demons in your name? Did we not perform many miracles in your name?”
And then I will declare to them, “I never knew you. Get away from me, you who practice lawlessness!”
So everyone who hears these words of mine and puts them into practice will be like a wise man who built his house on the rock.
The rain fell, the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house, but it did not fall, because it was firmly founded on the rock.
And everyone who hears these words of mine and does not put them into practice will be like a foolish man who built his house on the sand.
The rain fell, the rivers came, and the winds blew and struck that house. It fell, and its fall was great.
When Jesus finished these words, the crowds were amazed at his teaching.
For he taught them as someone who had authority, and not like their scribes.
As he came down from the mountain, large crowds followed him.
And look, a man with leprosy approached him and bowed down before him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
He stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I am willing. Be cleansed.” And immediately his leprosy was cleansed.
Jesus said to him, “See that you tell no one, but go, show yourself to the priest, and present your offering as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
When he entered Capernaum, a centurion approached him, pleading with him
and saying, “Lord, my son is lying at home, paralyzed and suffering terribly.”
Jesus said to him, “I will come and heal him.”
But the centurion answered, “Lord, I am not worthy for you to come under my roof. Just say the word, and he will recover.
For I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to this one, ‘Go,’ and he goes, and to another, ‘Come,’ and he comes, and to my slave, ‘Do this,’ and he does it.”
When Jesus heard this, he was amazed and said to those following him, “Truly I tell you, I have not found such great faith in anyone in Israel.
And I tell you that many will come from the east and the west and recline at the table with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.
But the children of the kingdom will be thrown out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there.”
Jesus said to the centurion, “Go. Let it happen for you as you have believed.” And his son recovered at that very hour.
Jesus came into Peter’s house and saw his mother-in-law lying down with a fever.
He touched her hand, and the fever left her. She got up and served him.
When evening came, they brought him many people who were possessed by demons. He cast out the unclean spirits with a word and healed everyone who was sick.
This was to fulfill what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet, who said, “He took our illnesses and bore our weaknesses.”
When Jesus saw a crowd around him, he gave orders to go to the other shore.
A scribe approached him and said to him, “Teacher, I will follow you wherever you go.”
Jesus said to him, “Foxes have their dens, and the birds of the sky have their nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
Another of the disciples said to him, “Lord, first allow me to go and bury my father.”
But Jesus said to him, “Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.”
When he got into the boat, his disciples followed him.
And look, a great storm arose on the sea, so that the boat was covered by the waves. But he was asleep.
They approached him and woke him, saying, “Lord, save us! We are going to die!”
He said to them, “Why are you afraid, you of little faith?” Then he got up and rebuked the winds and the sea, and there was a great calm.
The men were amazed and said, “What kind of man is this, that the winds and the sea obey him?”
When he came to the other shore, to the region of the Gerasenes, two men possessed by demons met him, coming out of the tombs. They were so fierce that no one could pass along that road.
And look, they cried out, saying, “What do you want with us, Jesus, Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the appointed time?”
Now there was a large herd of pigs some distance from them, being tended.
The demons begged him, saying, “If you are going to cast us out, send us into the herd of pigs.”
He said to them, “Go!” They came out and went into the pigs. And look, the whole herd rushed down the steep slope into the sea and died in the water.
Those tending them fled and went into the town. They reported everything, including what had happened to the people possessed by demons.
And look, the whole town came out to meet Jesus. When they saw him, they begged him to leave their territory.
He got into the boat, crossed over, and came to his own town.
And look, they brought him a paralyzed man lying on a bed. When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralyzed man, “Take courage, my son. Your sins are forgiven.”
And look, some of the scribes said to themselves, “This man is blaspheming.”
But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to them, “Why do you think evil things in your hearts?”
For which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?
But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—then he said to the paralyzed man, “Get up, pick up your bed, and go home.”
He got up and went home.
When the crowds saw this, they were afraid and gave glory to God, who had given such authority to human beings.
As Jesus went on from that place, he saw a man named Matthew sitting at his tax booth. He said to him, “Follow me.” He got up and followed him.
While he was reclining at the table in his house, many tax collectors and sinners came and reclined with Jesus and his disciples.
When the Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples, “Why does your teacher eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
When he heard this, he said, “It is not the healthy who need a doctor, but those who are sick.
Go and learn what this means: ‘I want mercy rather than sacrifice.’ For I did not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
Then John’s disciples came to him and said, “Why do we and the Pharisees fast often, but your disciples do not fast?”
Jesus said to them, “Can the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them? But days are coming when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then they will fast.
No one puts a patch of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, for it will pull away the surrounding part of the garment, and a large tear will result.

Nor do people put new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the wineskins burst, the wine spills out, and the wineskins are ruined. Instead, they put new wine into new wineskins, and both are preserved.”
While he was saying these things to them, look, a ruler approached him and bowed down before him, saying, “My daughter has just died, but come and lay your hand on her, and she will live.”
Jesus got up and followed him, along with his disciples.
A woman who had suffered from bleeding for twelve years came up behind him and touched the edge of his garment.
For she was saying to herself, “If I only touch the edge of his garment, I will be healed.”
Jesus turned and saw her. He said to her, “Take courage, my daughter. Your faith has saved you.” And the woman was healed from that moment.
When Jesus came into the ruler’s house, he saw the flute players and the crowd making a commotion.
He said, “Go away, for the little girl has not died but is sleeping.” But they laughed at him, knowing that she had died.
After the crowd had been put outside, he went in and took her hand, and the little girl got up.
News about him spread throughout that whole region.
As Jesus went on from that place, two blind men followed him, shouting, “Have mercy on us, Jesus, Son of David!”
When he entered the house, the blind men came to him. Jesus said to them, “Do you believe that I can do this?” They said to him, “Yes, Lord.”
Then he touched their eyes and said, “Let it happen to you according to your faith.”
And their eyes were opened. Jesus commanded them sternly, saying, “See that no one finds out.”
But they went out and spread the news about him throughout that whole region.
As he was coming out, they brought him a man who could not speak and was possessed by a demon.
When he had cast out the demon, the man who could not speak spoke. The crowds were amazed and said, “Nothing like this has ever appeared in Israel.”
But the Pharisees were saying, “He casts out demons through the ruler of the demons.”
Jesus went around all the towns and villages, teaching in their synagogues, proclaiming the good news of the kingdom, and healing every disease and every illness.
When he saw the crowds, he had compassion on them, because they were troubled and cast down, like sheep without a shepherd.
Then he said to his disciples, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few.
So ask the Lord of the harvest to send out workers into his harvest.
He called his twelve disciples and gave them authority over unclean spirits, to cast them out and to heal every disease and every illness.
These are the names of the twelve apostles: first, Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew his brother; James the son of Zebedee and John his brother;
Philip and Bartholomew; Thomas and Matthew the tax collector; James the son of Alphaeus and Thaddaeus;
Simon the Cananaean and Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him.
Jesus sent out these twelve and instructed them, saying, “Do not go along a road to the Gentiles, and do not enter a Samaritan town.
Instead, go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
As you go, proclaim, ‘Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has drawn near.’
Heal the sick, cleanse those with leprosy, and cast out demons. You received freely; give freely.
Do not acquire gold or silver or copper for your belts,
or a bag for the journey, or two tunics, or sandals, or a staff, for the worker deserves his food.
Whatever town or village you enter, find out who is worthy there, and stay there until you leave.
As you enter the house, greet it.
If the house is worthy, let your peace come upon it; but if it is not worthy, let your peace return to you.
If anyone will not welcome you or listen to your words, shake the dust off your feet as you leave that house or town or village.
Truly I tell you, it will be easier for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for that town.
Look, I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. So be wise like snakes and innocent like doves.
But beware of people, for they will hand you over to councils and whip you in their synagogues.
They will bring you before governors and kings because of me, as a testimony to them and to the Gentiles.
When they hand you over, do not worry about how to speak or what to say, for what you are to say will be given to you at that time.
For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks through you.
A brother will hand over his brother to death, and a father his child. Children will rise up against their parents and put them to death.
Everyone will hate you because of my name, but whoever endures to the end will be saved.
When they persecute you in this town, flee to another. For truly I tell you, you will not finish going through the towns of Israel before the Son of Man comes.
For no disciple is greater than his teacher, and no slave is higher than his master.
It is enough for the disciple to be like his teacher, and the slave to be like his master. If they called the master Beelzebul, how much more will they call the members of his household that!
So do not be afraid of them. For nothing is covered that will not be uncovered, and nothing is hidden that will not be revealed.
What I tell you in the darkness, say in the light, and what you hear in your ear, proclaim from the rooftops.
Do not be afraid of those who kill your body but cannot kill your soul. Instead, be more afraid of the one who can destroy your soul and your body in Gehenna.
Are not two sparrows sold for an obol? Yet not one of them will fall to the ground without your Father in heaven.
Even the hairs of your head are all counted.
So do not be afraid of them. You are worth more than many sparrows.
Everyone who acknowledges me before people, I too will acknowledge before my Father in heaven.
But whoever denies me before people, I too will deny before my Father in heaven.
Do not think that I came to bring peace to the earth. I did not come to bring peace, but to bring a sword.
For I came to separate a man from his father, a daughter from her mother, and a daughter-in-law from her mother-in-law.
A person's enemies are the members of his own household.
Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me, and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me.
And whoever does not take up his cross and follow me is not worthy of me.
Whoever has found his life will lose it, and whoever has lost his life for my sake will find it.
Whoever welcomes you welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me.
Whoever welcomes a prophet because he is a prophet will receive a prophet's reward, and whoever welcomes a righteous person because he is righteous will receive the righteous person's reward.
And whoever gives one of these little ones even a cup of cold water to drink because he is a disciple—truly I tell you, he will not lose his reward.
When Jesus had finished giving instructions to his twelve disciples, he left that place to teach and preach in their towns.
When John heard in prison about the works of Christ, he sent a message through his disciples.
He said to them, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we wait for someone else?”
Jesus answered them, “Go and tell John what you hear and what you see:
the blind see, the lame walk, those with leprosy are cleansed, the deaf hear, the mute speak, the dead rise, and the poor have the good news proclaimed to them.”
And blessed is anyone who does not stumble because of me.
When they had gone, Jesus began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?”
But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothing? Look, those who wear soft clothing are in kings' houses.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, he is more than a prophet.
For this is the one about whom it is written: “Look, I will send my messenger ahead of you, who will prepare your way before you.”
Truly I tell you, among those born of women, no one has arisen who is greater than John the Baptist. Yet the one who is less than he is greater than he in the kingdom of heaven.
From the days of John the Baptist until now, the kingdom of heaven has been taken by force, and violent people seize it.
For all the prophets and the Law prophesied until John.
And if you are willing to accept it, he is Elijah, who is to come.
Let anyone who has ears to hear listen.
But to whom shall I compare this generation? It is like little children sitting in the marketplaces, calling to their companions
and saying, ‘We played the flute for you, but you did not dance. We sang a lament, but you did not mourn.’
For John came neither eating nor drinking, and they said, ‘He has a demon.’
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they said, ‘Look, a glutton and a wine drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’ Yet wisdom has been shown to be right by her deeds.
Then Jesus began to rebuke the cities where most of his miracles had taken place, because they had not repented.
‘Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that took place among you had taken place in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented in sackcloth and ashes.
But I tell you, it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon on the day of judgment than for you.

And you, Capernaum, will you be raised up to heaven? You will go down to the realm of the dead. For if the miracles that took place in you had taken place in Sodom and Gomorrah, they would have remained until this day.
But I tell you, it will be more bearable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrah on the day of judgment than for you.’

At that time Jesus responded, saying, ‘I praise you, my Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and the learned, but have revealed them to little children.
Yes, my Father, because this was pleasing in your sight.
Everything has been given to me by my Father. No one knows the Son except the Father, and no one knows the Father except the Son and anyone to whom the Son wishes to wish to reveal him.
Come to me, all who are weary and burdened, and I will give you rest.
Take my yoke upon you and learn from me, because I am gentle and humble in heart, and you will find rest for your souls.
For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.’
At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry and began to pluck heads of grain and eat.
When the Pharisees saw this, they said to him, ‘Look, your disciples are doing what is not lawful to do on the Sabbath.’
But he said to them, ‘Have you not read what David did when he and those with him were hungry?
How he entered the house of God and ate the bread of the offering, which neither he nor those with him were permitted to eat, but only the priests?
Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple break the Sabbath, and there is no guilt in this?
But I tell you that one greater than the temple is here.
If you had understood what “I want mercy rather than sacrifice” means, you would not have condemned those who are innocent.
For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.’
He left that place and entered their synagogue.
And look, there was a man whose hand was withered. They asked him about it, saying, “Is it lawful to heal him on the Sabbath?” so that they could accuse him.
But he said to them, “Which of you, if he has just one sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out?
How much more valuable a person is than a sheep! So it is lawful to do good on the Sabbath.”
Then he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and it became healthy like the other one.
But the Pharisees went out and plotted against him, so that they could kill him.
When Jesus learned of this, he withdrew from that place. A large crowd followed him, and he healed them all.
He sternly warned them not to make him known,
so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet would be fulfilled, when he said:
“Look, here is my son whom I have chosen, my beloved, in whom my soul delights. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will establish justice for the nations.
He will not quarrel or shout, and no one will hear his voice in the streets.
He will not break a bruised reed, and he will not put out a smoldering wick, until he brings his judgment forth in victory,
and the nations will put their hope in his name.”
Then they brought him a blind man who could not speak and was possessed by a demon. He healed him, so that the man who could not speak could speak and see.
All the crowds were amazed and said, “Could this be the Son of David?”
But when the Pharisees heard this, they said, “This man casts out demons only by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”
But he knew their thoughts and said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself becomes desolate, and no city or household divided against itself will stand.
If Satan too casts out Satan, then he is divided against himself. How, then, will his kingdom stand?
And if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
But if I cast out demons by the Spirit of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
Or who can enter the strong man's house and seize his belongings unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he can plunder his house.
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
Therefore I tell you that every sin and every blasphemy will be forgiven you people, but blasphemy against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
And whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks a word against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the one to come.
Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad, for a tree is known by its fruit.
You offspring of vipers! How can you say good things when you are evil? For the mouth speaks from what fills the heart.”
A good person brings good things out of his good store, and an evil person brings evil things out of his evil store.
I tell you that people will have to account for every idle word they speak on the day of judgment.
For by your words you will be justified, and by your words you will be condemned.
Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him, saying, “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”
But he answered them, saying, “An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.”
For just as Jonah was inside the sea monster for three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth for three days and three nights.
The people of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah’s preaching. And look, someone greater than Jonah is here.

The [?] of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon’s wisdom. And look, here is someone greater than Solomon!
When an unclean spirit comes out of a person, it passes through waterless places, seeking a place to rest, but finds none.
Then it says, “I will return to my house, the place I came out of.” When it comes, it finds it swept and put in order.

Then it goes and takes with it seven other spirits more evil than itself. They enter and live there, and that person’s last condition becomes worse than his first. That is how it will be with this evil generation.
While he was still speaking to the crowds, look! There were his mother and his brothers, standing outside, seeking to speak with him.
But he answered the person who was speaking to him, saying, “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”
He stretched out his hand toward his disciples, saying, “Look! Here are my mother and my brothers.”
For whoever does the will of my Father in heaven is my brother and sister and mother.
On that day he went out—Jesus went out of the house and sat beside the sea.
Large crowds gathered around him, so that he got into the boat and sat down, while the whole crowd stood on the shore.
He spoke the message to them through parables, saying, “Look! The sower went out to sow.”
As he sowed, some seeds fell beside the road, and the birds of the sky came and ate them.
Others fell on rocky places where there was not much soil. They sprouted immediately because there was little soil beneath them.
But when the sun rose, they were scorched, and because they had no root, they dried up.
Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up and choked them.
Others fell on good soil and produced fruit: one yielded a hundred, another sixty, and another thirty.
Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.
His disciples came to him and said, “Why do you speak to them in parables?”
He said to them, “You have been given the ability to understand the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but they have not been given it.”
For whoever has will be given more and will have an abundance, but whoever does not have will have even what he has taken away from him.
This is why I speak to them in parables: though they look, they do not see, and though they listen, they do not hear or understand.
The prophecy of Isaiah will be fulfilled in them, which says, “You will indeed hear, but not understand, and you will indeed see, but not perceive.”

For Pilate’s heart has grown dull, and they have heard with difficulty with their ears, and they have closed their eyes, so that they will not see with their eyes, hear with their ears, understand with their heart, and turn back, and I heal them.
Blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear.
For truly I tell you that many prophets and righteous people longed to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear me [?] what you hear, but did not hear it.
But you, listen to the parable of the sower.
Whenever anyone hears the word of the kingdom and does not understand it, the evil one comes and snatches away what was sown in his heart. This is the one sown beside the road.
The one sown on rocky places is the person who hears the word and immediately receives it with joy.
But he has no root within him and lasts only a short time. When trouble or persecution comes because of the word, he immediately falls away.
The one sown among the thorns is the person who hears the word, but the worry of this age and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the word, and he becomes unfruitful.
The one sown on good soil is the person who hears the word and understands it and bears fruit: one produces a hundredfold, another sixtyfold, and another thirtyfold.
He set another parable before them, saying, “The kingdom of heaven is like a man who sowed good seed in his field.”
But while the people were sleeping, his enemy came and sowed weeds among the wheat and went away.
When the plants grew and produced grain, then the weeds also appeared.
The servants approached their master and said to him, “Master, was it not good seed that you sowed in your field? Where, then, did it get weeds?”
But he said to them, “An enemy has done this.” They said to him, “Then do you want us to go and gather them up?”
But he said to them, “No, lest, while gathering the weeds, you uproot the wheat along with them.”
Leave them alone to grow together until harvest time. At harvest time I will tell my reapers, “Gather the weeds first and tie them in bundles to burn them, but gather the wheat into my storehouse.”
Again he set another parable before them, saying, “The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed that a man took and sowed in his field.”
It is smaller than all the seeds, but when it grows, it becomes a large garden plant and becomes a large tree, so that the birds of the sky come and settle in its branches.
He told them another parable, saying, “The kingdom of heaven is like yeast that a woman took and hid in three measures of flour until all of it was leavened.”
Jesus said all these things to the crowds in parables, and he said nothing to them without a parable.
This was so that what was spoken through the prophet might be fulfilled: “I will open my mouth in parables and speak of things hidden since the creation of the world.”
Then he left the crowds and went into the house. His disciples approached him, saying, “Explain to us the parable of the weeds in the field.”
He answered, saying, “The one who sows the good seed is the Son of Man.”
The field is the world. The good seed is the children of the kingdom, and the weeds are the children of the evil one.
The enemy who sowed them is the devil. The harvest is the end of the age, and the reapers are the angels.
Just as the weeds are gathered and burned in a fire, so it will be at the end of the age.
The Son of Man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom everything that causes people to stumble and those who practice lawlessness.
They will throw them into the fiery furnace. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there.
Then the righteous will shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom. Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear.
The kingdom of heaven is like a treasure hidden in a field. A man found it and hid it, and in his joy he goes and sells everything he owns and buys that field.
Again, the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant looking for fine pearls.
When he found a pearl of great value, he went and sold everything he had and bought it for himself.
The kingdom of heaven is like a net thrown into the sea that gathered fish of every kind.
When it was full, they pulled it up and sat down on the shore. They gathered the good fish into their containers, but threw the bad ones away.
This is how it will be at the end of the age. The angels will come out and separate the wicked from among the righteous.
They will throw them into the fiery furnace. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there.
“Have you understood all these things?” They said, “Yes, Lord.”
He said to them, “Therefore, every scribe who has been instructed in the kingdom of heaven is like a rich man who brings new things and old things out of his treasure.”
When Jesus had finished these parables, he left that place.
He came to his hometown and taught [?] them in their synagogue, so that they were amazed and said, “Where did this man get this wisdom and these miraculous powers?”
“Isn't this the carpenter's son? Isn't his mother called Mary, and aren't his brothers James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?”
“And his sisters [?] Simon—aren't they all here with us? Where, then, did this man get all these things?”
They took offense at him. But Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not despised except in his own hometown and in his own household.”
He did not perform many miracles there because of their unbelief.
At that time, Herod the tetrarch heard the reports about Jesus.
He said to his servants, “This is John the Baptist. He has risen from the dead, and that is why these miraculous powers are at work in him.”
For at that time Herod had seized John, bound him, and put him in prison because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip.
For John had been telling him, “It is not lawful for you to marry her.”
He wanted to kill him, but he was afraid of the crowd because they regarded him as a prophet.
When Herod’s birthday came, the daughter of Herodias danced among the guests and pleased Herod.
And he promised with an oath to give her whatever she asked for.
Prompted by her mother, she said, “Give me the head of John the Baptist here on a platter.”
The king was deeply distressed, but because of his oaths and those dining with him, he ordered that it be given to her.
He sent someone and had John beheaded in prison.
It was brought on the platter and given to the girl, and she brought it to her mother.
His disciples came, took his body, and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus.
When Jesus heard, he withdrew from there in a boat to a deserted place by himself. But when the crowds heard, they followed him on foot from the towns.
He came out and saw a large crowd. He had compassion on them and healed those among them who were sick.

When evening came, his disciples approached him and said, “This is a deserted place, and it is already late. Send the crowds away so that they can go to the surrounding villages and buy themselves something to eat.”
But Jesus said to them, “They do not need to go away. You give them something to eat.”
They said to him, “We have nothing here except five loaves of bread and two fish.”
He said to them, “Bring them here to me.”

He ordered the crowds to sit down on the grass. He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, and broke them. He gave the loaves to his disciples, and the disciples gave them to the crowds.
They all ate and were satisfied, and they gathered up the pieces left over, twelve full baskets.
Those who ate were about five thousand men, not counting children and women.
Immediately he made his disciples get into the boat and go ahead of him to the other shore while he dismissed the crowds.
After dismissing the crowds, he went up the mountain by himself and prayed. When evening came, he was there alone.
The boat was many stadia away from the shore, battered by the waves, because the wind was against them.
During the fourth watch of the night, he came to them, walking on the sea.
When they saw him walking on the sea, they were alarmed and said, “It is a ghost!” And they cried out in fear.
Immediately he spoke to them, saying, “Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.”
Peter answered him, saying, “Lord, if it is you, command me to come to you on the water.”
He said to him, “Come.” Peter got down out of the boat, walked on the water, and came to Jesus.
But when he saw the wind, he became afraid. As he began to sink, he cried out, “Lord, save me!”
Immediately Jesus stretched out his hand and caught him. He said to him, “You of little faith, why did you doubt?”
When they got into the boat, the wind stopped immediately.
Those in the boat worshiped him, saying, “Truly, you are the Son of God.”
When they had crossed over, they came ashore at Gennesaret.
The people of that place recognized him and sent word throughout the whole surrounding region. They brought everyone who was sick to him.
They begged him to let them touch just the edge of his clothing, and those who touched it were healed.
Then some Pharisees and scribes from Jerusalem came to Jesus, saying,
“Why do your disciples break the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they are going to eat their bread.”
He answered them, saying, “Why do you yourselves break God's commandment because of your tradition?”
“For God said, ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ and, ‘Whoever speaks evil of his father or his mother must be put to death.’
“But you say that whoever tells his father or his mother, ‘Whatever you would have benefited from me is a gift,’
“will not honor his father. You have set aside God's word because of your tradition.
“You hypocrites! Isaiah rightly prophesied about you when he said,
‘[?] honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
‘They worship me in vain, teaching human commandments as doctrines.’
He called the crowd and said to them, “Listen and understand.”
“It is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a person, but what comes out of the mouth defiles a person.”
Then his disciples came to him and said, “Do you know that the Pharisees were offended when they heard these words?”
He answered them, saying, “Every plant that my Father in heaven has not planted will be uprooted.
“Leave them alone. They are blind guides. If a blind person leads another blind person, both will fall into a pit.”
Peter responded by saying to him, “Explain the parable to us.”
He said to them, “Are you yourselves also without understanding?
“Do you not understand that everything that goes into the mouth goes down into the stomach and is expelled into the latrine?
“But the things that come out of the mouth come from the heart, and those are what defile a person.
“For from the heart come evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, sexual immorality, thefts, false testimony, and slander.
“These are what defile a person, but eating without washing your hands does not defile a person.”
He left that place and withdrew to the regions of Tyre and Sidon.
Look, a Canaanite woman came out from those regions and cried out, saying, “Have mercy on me, Lord, Son of David! My daughter is suffering terribly.”
But he did not answer her a word. His disciples approached him and begged him, saying, “Send her away, because she keeps crying out behind us.”
But he answered, saying, “I was sent to no one except the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”
But she approached him, bowing down before him and saying, “Lord, help me.”
But he answered her, saying, “It is not right to take the children’s bread and throw it to their dogs.”
But she said, “Yes, Lord, even the dogs eat the crumbs that fall from their masters’ table.”
Then he answered her, saying, “Woman, your faith is great! Let it happen for you as you wish.” And her daughter was healed from that hour.
When Jesus left that place, he came to the Sea of Galilee. He went up the mountain and sat down there.
Large crowds approached him, bringing with them blind people, people who could not walk, people who could not speak, people with crippled limbs, and many others. They laid them at his feet.

The crowds were amazed when they saw people who could not walk walking, people with crippled limbs healed, people who could not speak speaking, and blind people seeing. And they gave glory to the God of Israel.

Jesus called his disciples and said to them, “I have compassion for this crowd, because they have stayed with me for three days now and have nothing to eat. I do not want to send them away hungry, in case they faint on the road.”
His disciples said to him, “Where will we find so much bread in this wilderness to feed such a large crowd?”
Jesus said to them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said to him, “Seven, and some small fish.”
He instructed the crowds to sit down on the ground.
He took the seven loaves and the fish, gave thanks over them, broke them, and gave them to his disciples. The disciples gave them to the crowds.
They all ate and were satisfied. They picked up the leftover pieces, seven full baskets.
Those who ate were four thousand men, besides little children and women.
After sending the crowds away, he got into the boat and came to the region of Magadan.
The Pharisees and Sadducees approached him to test him, asking him to show them a sign from heaven.
But he answered them, saying:
“An evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.” Then he left them behind and went away.
His disciples came to the other side and had forgotten to bring bread with them.
Jesus said to them, “Watch out and beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.”
They were thinking among themselves, saying, “We did not bring bread with us.”
When Jesus realized this, he said to them, “Why are you thinking among yourselves, you of little faith, that you did not bring bread with you?”
Do you still not understand? Do you not remember the five loaves for the five thousand people, and how many baskets you collected?
Nor the seven loaves for the four thousand, and how many baskets you collected?
How is it that you do not understand that I was not speaking to you about bread? But beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
Then they understood that he had not spoken to them about the yeast in bread, but about the teaching of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
When Jesus came to the [?] of Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, “Who do people say the Son of Man is?”
They said, “Some say he is John the Baptist; others say he is Elijah; still others say he is Jeremiah or one of the prophets.”
He said, “But you yourselves—who do you say I am?”
Simon Peter answered, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Jesus answered him, “Blessed are you, Simon Bar-Jonah, because flesh and blood did not reveal this to you, but my Father in heaven did.
And I too tell you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of the realm of the dead will not be able to overcome it.
I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven. Whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you release on earth will be released in heaven.”
Then he instructed his disciples not to tell anyone that he was the Christ.

From that time on, Jesus began to tell his disciples that he must go up to Jerusalem and suffer many things at the hands of the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and rise on the third day.
Peter took him aside and began to rebuke him, saying, “May you be spared, Lord! This will never happen to you.”
But he turned and said to Peter, “Get behind me, Satan! You are a stumbling block to me, because you are not thinking about the things of God, but the things of human beings.”
Then Jesus said to his disciples, “Whoever wants to come after me must deny himself and take up his cross.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, but whoever loses his life because of me will find it.
For what will a person gain if he gains the whole world but loses his life? Or what will a person give in exchange for his life?
For the Son of Man is coming in the glory of his Father with his angels, and he will repay each person according to their deeds.
For truly I tell you, some of those standing here will not taste death until they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.”
After six days, Jesus took Peter, James, and his brother John up onto a high mountain by themselves.
He was transformed before them. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white like the light.
Look! Moses and Elijah appeared to him, talking with him.
Peter said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to stay here. Do you want us to make three shelters here, one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah?”
While he was still speaking, look! A bright cloud overshadowed them, and a voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is my beloved Son, in whom I am pleased. Listen to him!”
When the disciples heard this, they fell on their faces and were very afraid.
Jesus came forward and touched them, saying, “Get up. Do not be afraid.”
When they looked up, they saw no one except Jesus alone.
As they were coming down the mountain, Jesus instructed them, saying, “Tell no one about the vision until the Son of Man rises from the dead.”
The disciples asked him, “Why, then, do the scribes say that Elijah must come first?”
He answered them, “Elijah is indeed coming, and he will restore everything.
I tell you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wanted. In the same way, the Son of [?] Man will also suffer at their hands.”
Then the disciples understood that he was speaking to them about John the Baptist.
When he came to the crowd, a man approached him, pleading with him
and saying, “Lord, have mercy on my son, because he has seizures and suffers badly. He often falls into the fire and often into the water.
I brought him to your disciples, but they were unable to heal him.”
Jesus answered, “You unbelieving and perverse generation! How long will I stay with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring him here to me.”
Jesus rebuked him, and the demon came out of him. The boy was healed from that moment.
Then the disciples approached Jesus privately and said to him, “Why were we unable to cast it out?”

He said to them, “Because of your little faith. For truly I tell you, if you have faith like a mustard seed, you will say to this mountain, ‘Move from here to there,’ and it will move. Nothing will be impossible for you.”
As they were traveling through Galilee, Jesus said to them, “The Son of Man will be handed over to human hands,
and they will kill him, and he will rise on the third day.” They were deeply grieved.
When they came to Capernaum, the tax collectors approached Peter and said, “Does your teacher not pay his tax?”

He said, “Yes.” When he entered the house, Jesus spoke to him first, saying, “What do you think, Simon? From whom do the kings of the earth collect duties or taxes? Do they collect them from their own children or from strangers?”
When he said, “From strangers,” Jesus said to him, “Then the children are exempt.”

But so that we do not offend them, go to the sea and cast a hook. Take the first fish that comes up, and when you open its mouth, you will find a stater coin. Take it and give it to them for me and you.
At that time the disciples approached Jesus and said, “Who, then, is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?”
Jesus called a little child and had him stand among them.
He said to them, “Truly I tell you, unless you turn and become like these little children, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.
Whoever humbles himself like this little child is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven.
And whoever welcomes a little child like this in my name welcomes me.
But whoever causes one of these little ones who believe in me to stumble would be better off having a millstone tied around his neck and being drowned in the depths of the sea.
Woe to the world because of the things that cause people to stumble! For these things must come, but woe to the person through whom they come!

If your hand or your foot causes you to stumble, cut it off and throw it away from you. For it is better for you to enter life lame or maimed than to have two hands or two feet and be thrown into the eternal fire.
And if your eye causes you to sin, tear it out and throw it away from you. For it is better for you to enter life with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into the fiery hell.
See that you do not despise one of these little ones. For I tell you that their angels in heaven always look upon the face of my Father in heaven.
What do you think? If a man has a hundred sheep and one of them goes astray, will he not leave the ninety-nine sheep on the mountains and go looking for the one that has strayed?
And if he finds it, truly I tell you, he rejoices over it more than over the ninety-nine that did not stray.
In the same way, it is not the will of my Father in heaven that one of these little ones should perish.
If your brother sins, go and correct him privately, between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have won back your brother.
But if he does not listen to you, take one or two others with you, so that every matter may be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses.
If he does not listen to them, tell the church. And if he refuses to listen even to the church, let him be to you like a Gentile and a tax collector.
Truly I tell you, whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you release on earth will be released in heaven.
Again, truly I tell you, if two of you agree with each other on earth about anything they ask for, it will be done for them by my Father in heaven.
For wherever two or three are gathered in my name, I am there with them, in their midst.
Then Peter came up to him and said, “Lord, if my brother sins against me, how many times should I forgive him? Up to seven times?”
Jesus said to him, “I do not tell you up to seven times, but up to seventy times seven.”
For this reason, the kingdom of heaven is like a king who wanted to settle accounts with his slaves.
When he began to settle accounts, someone who owed a great deal was brought to him.
Since he had nothing with which to pay, his master ordered him to be sold, along with his wife, his children, and everything he owned, so that payment could be made.
Then the slave fell down and bowed before him, saying, “Lord, be patient with me, and I will pay you everything.”
The slave’s master had compassion on him, released him, and forgave him everything he owed.
But that slave went out and found one of his fellow slaves who owed him a hundred staters. He seized him and began choking him, saying, “Pay what you owe!”
Then his fellow slave fell down and pleaded with him, saying, “Be patient with me, and I will pay you everything.”
But he refused. Instead, he went and threw him into prison until he paid what he owed.
When his fellow slaves saw what had happened, they were deeply distressed. They went and told their master everything that had happened.
Then his master summoned him and said to him, “You wicked slave! I forgave you everything you owed because you begged me.
Should you not also have had mercy on your fellow slave, just as I had mercy on you?”
His master became angry and handed him over to the torturers until he paid everything he owed.
This is also what my Father in heaven will do to you if each of you does not forgive his brother from your hearts.
When Jesus had finished these words, he left Galilee and came to the region of Judea on the other side of the Jordan.
Large crowds followed him, and he healed them there.
The Pharisees approached him to test him, saying, “Is a man allowed to divorce his wife for any reason?”
He answered, “Have you not read that the one who created them from the beginning made them male and female?
And for this reason a man will leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two will become one flesh.
So they are no longer two, but one flesh. Therefore, let no human being separate what God has joined together.”
They said to him, “Why, then, did Moses command us to give them a certificate of divorce and send them away?”
He said to them, “Because of your hard-heartedness, Moses allowed you to divorce your wives. But it was not this way from the beginning.
But I tell you that whoever divorces his wife, except on grounds of sexual immorality, and marries another woman commits adultery.”
His disciples said to him, “If this is the situation between a man and his wife, it is better not to marry.”
But he said to them, “Not everyone can accept this saying, but only those to whom it has been given.”

For there are eunuchs who were born that way from their mother’s womb, and there are eunuchs who were made eunuchs by other people, and there are eunuchs who made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven. Let anyone who can accept this accept it.
Then little children were brought to him so that he would lay his hands on them and pray. But the disciples rebuked them.
But Jesus said, “Let the little children come to me, and do not prevent them, for the kingdom of heaven belongs to those who are like them.”
He laid his hands on them and left that place.
Then someone approached him and said, “Good teacher, what must I do to receive eternal life?”
He said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one, God. But if you want to enter life, keep the commandments.”
He said to him, “Which ones?” He replied, “You must not murder. You must not commit adultery. You must not steal. You must not give false testimony.
Honor your father and your mother, and love your neighbor as yourself.”
The young man said to him, “I have kept all these since my childhood. What do I still lack?”
Jesus said to him, “If you want to be perfect, go and sell all your possessions and give them to the poor, and you will store up treasure for yourself in heaven. Then come and follow me.”
When the young man heard these words, he went away sad, because he had many possessions.
Jesus said to his disciples, “Truly I tell you, it is difficult for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.
Again I tell you, it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of heaven.”
When the disciples heard this, they were greatly astonished and said, “Then who can be saved?”
Jesus looked at them and said, “This is impossible for human beings, but nothing is impossible for God.”
Then Peter answered him, saying, “Look, we have left everything behind and followed you. What, then, will we receive?”

Jesus said to him, “Truly I tell you: you who have followed me, at the rebirth, when the Son of Man sits on the throne of his glory, will also sit on your twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
And everyone who has left behind a house, brother, sister, father, mother, wife, child, or field because of my name will receive them many times over and inherit eternal life.
But many who are first will be last, and the last will be first.
For the kingdom of heaven is like a rich man who went out early in the morning to hire workers for his vineyard.
He agreed with the workers on one stater a day and sent them into his vineyard.
He went out at the third hour and saw others standing idle in the marketplace.
He said to the others, ‘You too go into my vineyard, and I will give you whatever is fair.’
So they went. He went out again at the sixth and ninth hours and did the same.
When he went out again at the eleventh hour, he saw others standing there. He said to them, ‘Why are you standing here idle all day?’
They said to him, ‘Because no one has hired us.’ He said to them, ‘You too go into my vineyard.’
When evening came, the owner of the vineyard said to his manager, ‘Call the workers and pay them their wages, beginning with the last until you reach the first.’
Those hired at the eleventh hour came and received one stater each.
The first also came, thinking they would receive more, but they too received one stater each.
When they received it, they grumbled against the owner,
saying, ‘These last workers worked only one hour, and you have made them equal to us, who bore the burden of the day and the scorching heat.’
But he answered one of them, saying, ‘Friend, I am not treating you unjustly. Did I not agree with you on one stater?
Take what is yours and go. I want to give this last worker the same as you.
Or am I not allowed to do what I want with what is mine? Or are you envious because I am good?’
This is how the first will be last, and the last will be first.”
As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took his twelve disciples aside by themselves, and on the road he said to them,
“Look, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the Son of Man will be handed over to the chief priests and the scribes, and they will condemn him to death.
They will hand him over to the Gentiles to mock him, flog him, and crucify him, and he will rise on the third day.”
Then the mother of Zebedee’s sons approached him with her sons, bowing before him and asking him for something.
He said to her, “What do you want?” She said, “Say that these two sons of mine will sit, one at your right and one at your left, in your kingdom.”
Jesus answered, “You do not know what you are asking for. Can you drink the cup that I am going to drink?” They said to him, “Yes.”
He said to them, “You will indeed drink my cup, but to sit at my right or at my left is not mine to grant. It belongs to those for whom it has been prepared by my Father.”
When the ten heard this, they became indignant at the two brothers.
Jesus called them to him and said to them, “You know that the rulers of the nations lord it over them, and their great men exercise authority over them.
It is not this way among you. Rather, whoever wants to become great among you will be your servant.
And whoever wants to be first among you will be your slave,
just as the Son of Man did not come to be served, but to serve and to give his life as a ransom for many.”
As he was leaving Jericho, large crowds followed him.
And look, two blind men were sitting beside the road. When they heard that Jesus was passing by, they cried out, “Have mercy on us, Son of David!”
The crowds rebuked them, telling them to be quiet. But they cried out all the more, “Lord, have mercy on us, Son of David!”
Jesus stopped and called them, saying, “What do you want me to do for you?”
They said to him, “Lord, let our eyes be opened.”
Jesus had compassion on them and touched their eyes. Immediately they could see, and they followed him.
When they approached Jerusalem and came to Bethphage, at the Mount of Olives, Jesus sent two disciples,
saying to them, “Go into the village ahead of you, and immediately you will find a donkey tied up, with a colt beside her. Untie them and bring them to me.
If anyone says anything to you, say, ‘Their Lord needs them,’ and he will send them immediately.”
All this happened so that what was spoken through the prophet would be fulfilled:
“Tell the daughter of Zion, ‘Look, your king is coming to you. He is gentle, riding on a donkey and on a colt, the offspring of a beast of burden.’”
The disciples went and did as Jesus had instructed them.
They brought the donkey and the colt and put their cloaks on them, and he mounted them.
The large crowd spread their cloaks on the road, while others cut branches from the trees and spread them on the road.
The crowds walking ahead of him and those following him were crying out, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!”
When he entered Jerusalem, the whole city was stirred up, saying, “Who is this?”
The crowds were saying, “This is the prophet Jesus, from Nazareth in Galilee.”
When Jesus entered the temple, he drove out everyone selling and buying in the temple. He overturned the tables of the money changers and the seats of those selling doves.
He said to them, “It is written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer,’ but you have made it a den of robbers.”
Blind and lame people came to him in the temple, and he healed them.
When the chief priests and the scribes saw the wonders he had done and the little children shouting, “Hosanna to the Son of David!” they became indignant.
They said to him, “Do you hear what these children are saying?” Jesus said to them, “Yes. Have you never read, ‘From the mouths of little children and nursing infants you have prepared praise’?”
He left them and went outside the city to Bethany, and he stayed there.
In the morning, as he was returning to the city, he became hungry.
He saw a fig tree beside the road and went up to it, but he found nothing on it except leaves. He said to it, “May no fruit ever come from you again.” Immediately the fig tree withered.
When his disciples saw this, they were amazed and said, “How did the fig tree wither immediately?”

Jesus answered, “Truly I tell you, if you have faith and do not doubt, you will not only do what was done to the fig tree, but even if you say to this mountain, ‘Get up and go down into the sea,’ it will happen for you.
And everything you ask for in prayer, believing, you will receive.”

When he entered the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people approached him while he was teaching and said, “By what authority are you doing these things, and who gave you this authority?”
Jesus answered them, “I too will ask you one question. If you answer it for me, I too will tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
Where did John’s baptism come from? Was it from heaven or from people?” They reasoned among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Then why did you not believe him?’
