But if we say, ‘It is from human beings,’ we are afraid of the crowd, because everyone regards John as a prophet.
They answered Jesus, “We do not know.” He in turn said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.
What do you think? A man had two sons. He approached the first and said, ‘My son, go and work in my vineyard today.’
He answered, ‘No.’ But afterward he changed his mind and went.
He also approached the other son and said the same thing to him. He answered, ‘I will go, sir,’ but he did not go.
Which of the two did his father’s will?” They said to him, “The first.” Jesus said to them, “Truly I tell you, tax collectors and prostitutes are going into the kingdom of God ahead of you.

For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you did not believe him. But the tax collectors and prostitutes believed him. Even after you saw this, you did not change your minds and believe him.
Listen to another parable. A rich man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug a winepress in it, and built a tower. He entrusted it to farmers and went away.
When the harvest season drew near, he sent his servants to the farmers to collect his fruit.
Those farmers seized his servants. They beat one, killed another, and stoned another.
Again he sent other servants, more than the first, and they treated them in the same way.
Afterward he sent his son to them, saying, “They will respect my son.”
But the farmers said among themselves, ‘This is the heir. Come, let us kill him and take his inheritance.’
They seized him, threw him outside the vineyard, and killed him.
So when the owner of the vineyard comes, what will he do to those farmers?”
They said to him, “He will utterly destroy those wicked men and give the vineyard to other tenant farmers who will give him its fruit at the proper times.”
Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the Scriptures: ‘The stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone. This came about through the Lord, and it is wonderful in your eyes’?”
“Therefore I tell you that the kingdom of God will be taken away from you and given to a nation that produces its fruit.”
“Whoever falls on this stone will be broken, and whoever the stone falls on, it will crush.”
When the chief priests and the Pharisees heard his parables, they realized that he was speaking about them.
Although they were looking for a way to arrest him, they were afraid of the crowds, because the crowds regarded him as a prophet.
Again Jesus responded and spoke to them in parables, saying:
“The kingdom of heaven is like a king who held a wedding feast for his son.”
“He sent his servants out to call those invited to the wedding feast, but they did not want to come.”

“Again he sent many other servants, saying, ‘Tell those who have been invited: Look, I have prepared my meal. My cattle and fattened animals have been slaughtered, and everything is ready. Come to the wedding feast.’”
But they paid no attention and went away, some to their fields and another to his business.
The rest seized his servants, mistreated them, and killed them.
“The king became angry and sent his troops, destroyed those murderers, and burned their city.”
“Then he said to his servants, ‘The wedding hall is ready, but those who were invited were not worthy.’”
“‘So go out to the crossroads and invite everyone you find to the wedding hall.’”
“Those servants went out into the roads and brought in everyone they found, both bad and good, and the wedding hall was filled with guests reclining at the meal.”
“When the king came in to see the guests reclining at the meal, he saw a man there who was not wearing wedding clothes.”
“He said to him, ‘Friend, how did you come in here without wearing wedding clothes?’ But he was speechless.”
“The king said to the attendants, ‘Tie his hands and feet and throw him out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there.’”
“For many are called, but few are chosen.”
Then the Pharisees went and made a plan to trap him in something he said.

They sent their disciples to him with the Herodians, saying, “Teacher, we know that you are truthful and teach the way of God truthfully. You are not concerned about anyone’s opinion, for you do not judge people by their status.”
“So tell us what you think: Is it lawful to pay the tax to the king, or is it not lawful?”
But Jesus, recognizing their wickedness, said to them, “Why are you testing me, you hypocrites?”
“Show me the coin used for the tax.” They brought him a stater.
He said to them, “Whose image and inscription are these?”
They said to him, “The king’s.” Then he said to them, “So give the king what belongs to the king, and God what belongs to God.”
When they heard this, they were amazed, and they left him and went away.
On that day the Sadducees, who say there will be no resurrection, came to him and questioned him,
saying, “Teacher, Moses said, ‘If someone dies without having children, his brother must marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.’
Now there were seven brothers among us. The first married and died, and since he had no children, he left his wife to his brother.
The same happened to the second and the third, down to the seventh.
After them all, the woman died.
So in the resurrection, whose wife will she be among the seven? For they all married her.”
Jesus answered and said to them, “You are mistaken because you do not know the Scriptures or the power of God.
For in the resurrection they neither take wives nor live with husbands, but they will be like the angels in heaven.
But concerning the resurrection of the dead, have you not read what was spoken to you by God, who said,
‘I am the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob’? He is not the God of the dead, but of the living.”
When the crowds heard this, they were amazed at his teaching.
When the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they gathered together.
One of them, an expert in the law, questioned him to test him.
“Teacher, which is the greatest commandment in the Law?”
He said to him, “You must love the Lord your God with all your heart, with all your soul, and with all your thoughts.
This is the greatest and first commandment.
The second, which is like it, is this: ‘You must love your neighbor as yourself.’
The Law and the Prophets depend on these two commandments.”
While the Pharisees were gathered together, Jesus questioned them,
saying, “What do you think about the Christ? Whose son is he?” They said to him, “He is David’s son.”
He said to them, “How, then, does David, speaking by the Spirit, call him Lord, saying,
‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies beneath your feet”’?
If David calls him Lord, how is he his son?”
No one could answer him a word, nor did anyone dare to question him from that day on.
Then Jesus spoke to the crowds and his disciples.
He said, “The scribes and the Pharisees have taken their seats in Moses’ seat.
Do everything they tell you and observe it, but do not act according to their deeds, for they speak but do not act.
They tie up heavy burdens that are difficult to carry and place them on people’s necks, but they themselves are unwilling to move them with even one of their fingers.
They do everything they do so that people will see them. For they widen their scripture boxes and make their tassels large.
They love the places of honor at banquets and the front seats in the synagogues,
and greetings in the marketplaces, and being called ‘Rabbi’ by people.
But you must not let yourselves be called Rabbi, for you have one teacher, and you are all brothers.
And do not call anyone on earth your father, for you have one Father, who is in heaven.
Nor should you let yourselves be called teachers, for you have one teacher, Christ.
The greatest among you will be your servant.
Whoever exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
But woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you shut the kingdom of heaven in people’s faces. You yourselves do not enter, nor do you allow those who are entering to go in.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel across sea and dry land to make one convert, and when he becomes one, you make him a child of hell twice as much as yourselves.
Woe to you, blind guides, who say, ‘Whoever swears by the temple, it means nothing, but whoever swears by the gold of the temple is bound by his oath.’
You fools and blind people! For which is greater: the gold or the temple that makes the gold holy?
And you say, ‘Whoever swears by the altar, it means nothing, but whoever swears by the offering on it is bound by his oath.’
You fools and blind people! For which is greater: the offering or the altar that makes the offering holy?
So whoever swears by the altar swears by it and by what rests upon it.
And whoever swears by the temple swears by it and by the one who dwells in it.
And whoever swears by heaven swears by God’s throne and by the one seated upon it.

Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you give a tenth of mint, dill, and cumin, but you have neglected the weightier matters of the law: justice, mercy, and faith. You should have practiced these without neglecting the others.
You blind guides, who strain out the gnat but swallow the camel!
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but their inside is full of robbery and impurity.
Blind Pharisee! First clean the inside of the cup and the dish so that their outside may also become clean.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you are like whitewashed tombs, which are beautiful on the outside, but inside are full of dead people’s bones and every kind of impurity.
You too are like this: on the outside you appear righteous to people, but your inside is full of hypocrisy and lawlessness.
Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you build the tombs of the prophets and decorate the graves of the righteous.
You say, ‘If we had lived in the days of our ancestors, we would not have joined them in shedding the blood of the prophets.’
So you testify against yourselves that you are children of those who killed the prophets.
You yourselves have filled up the measure of your ancestors.
You snakes, children of vipers! How will you escape condemnation to hell?
Therefore, look! I will send you prophets, wise people, and scribes. You will kill and crucify some of them, and flog some of them in your synagogues and pursue them from city to city.
So that all the righteous blood shed on the earth may come upon you, from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom you killed between the temple and the altar.
Truly I tell you, all these things will come upon this generation.
Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I wanted to gather your children together, as a bird gathers its young under its wings, but you were unwilling.
Look! Your house is left to you.
I tell you, you will not see me from now on until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.’
Jesus came out of the temple and went away. His disciples approached him to point out the temple buildings to him.
He answered them, ‘Do you see all these things? Truly I tell you, not one stone will be left upon another here without being torn down.’
As he sat on the Mount of Olives, the disciples approached him privately, saying, ‘Tell us, when will these things happen, and what will be the sign of your coming and the end of the age?’
Jesus answered them, ‘Be careful that no one leads you astray.’
For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am the Christ,’ and they will lead many astray.
You will hear of wars and reports of wars. Be careful not to be alarmed, for these things must happen, but the end has not yet come.
For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be famines and earthquakes in various places.
But all these things are the beginning of the birth pains.
Then they will hand you over to suffering and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations because of my name.
Then many will fall away, betray one another, and hate one another.
Many false prophets will arise and lead many people astray.
Because lawlessness increases, the love of many will grow cold.
But the one who endures to the end will be saved.
This good news of the kingdom will be proclaimed throughout the whole inhabited world as a testimony to all nations. Then the end will come.
But when you see the abomination that causes desolation, spoken of through the prophet Daniel, standing in the holy place—let the reader understand—
Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains.
The one on the roof must not come down to take the things in his house.
And anyone in the field must not turn back to get his garment.
But woe to those who are pregnant and those who are nursing babies in those days!
Pray that your flight will not happen in winter or on the Sabbath.
For at that time there will be great suffering, unlike anything that has happened since the beginning of the world until now, and nothing like it will ever happen again.
And unless those days were shortened, no one would survive. But for the sake of the chosen ones, those days will be shortened.
Then if anyone says to you, 'Look, the Christ is here!' or 'This is he!' do not believe it.
For many false Christs and false prophets will arise and perform great signs and wonders, so as to lead even the chosen ones astray, if possible.
Look, I have told you beforehand.
But if they say to you, 'Look, he is in the wilderness!' do not go out. 'Look, he is in the inner rooms!' do not believe it.
For just as lightning comes from the east and shines as far as the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
Wherever the body is, the eagles will gather around it.
Immediately after the suffering of those days, the sun will become dark, and the moon will not give its light. The stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky, and then all the tribes of the earth will see, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.
And he will send out his angels with a loud trumpet blast, and they will gather his chosen ones from the four winds, from one end of the heavens to the other.
Learn the lesson from the fig tree: when its branch becomes tender and its leaves sprout, you know that summer is near.
It is the same with you: when you see all these things, know that he is near, at the doors.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away before all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
But no one knows about that day and hour, not even the angels of heaven, only the Father alone.
For just as it was in the days of Noah, so will the coming of the Son of Man be.
For in those days before the flood, they were eating and drinking, taking wives and living with husbands, until the day Noah entered the ark.
And they did not understand until the flood came and swept everyone away. So will the coming of the Son of Man be.
Then two will be in the field; one will be taken and one will be left.
Two women will be grinding at a mill; one will be taken and one will be left.
So keep watch, because you do not know on what day the Lord is coming.
But understand this: if the master of the house had known during which watch of the night the thief was coming, he would have stayed awake and would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
Therefore you too must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not expect.
Who, then, is the faithful and wise servant whom his master has put in charge of his servants to give them their food at the proper time?
Blessed is that servant whom his master finds doing this when he comes.
Truly I say that he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
But if the wicked servant says in his heart, “My master will be late in coming,”
and begins to beat his fellow servants and to eat and drink with those who are drunk,
that servant’s master will come on a day when he is not expecting him and at an hour he does not know,
and will cut him in two and assign him his place with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there.
Then the kingdom of heaven will be like ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
Five of them were foolish, and five were wise.
For the foolish ones took their lamps but did not take oil with them.
But the wise ones took oil in their containers along with their lamps.
When the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
But at midnight a cry rang out: “Look, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!”
Then all those virgins got up and put their lamps in order.
The foolish ones said to the wise ones, “Give us some of your oil, because our lamps are going out.”
But the wise ones answered, “There may not be enough for both us and you. Go instead to those who sell it and buy some for yourselves.”
While they were going to buy it, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding hall, and the door was shut.
Afterward the remaining virgins came, saying, “Lord, open the door for us!”
But he answered, “Truly I tell you, I do not know you.”
Therefore stay awake, because you do not know the day or the hour.
For it is like a man who was about to travel abroad: he called his servants and entrusted all his possessions to them.
To one he gave five talents, to another two, and to another one, to each according to his ability. Then he went abroad.
Immediately the one who had received the five talents went and traded with them and gained another five.
Likewise, the one with the two gained another two.
But the one who had received the one talent went away, dug in the ground, and buried his master's money.
After a long time, the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them.
The one who had received the five talents came forward and brought him five more talents, saying, “Master, you gave me five talents. Look, I have gained five more.”
His master said to him, “Well done, good and faithful servant. Since you were trustworthy with a few things, I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into your master's joy.”
The one with the two talents came forward, saying, “Master, you gave me two talents. Look, I have gained two more.”
His master said to him, “Well done, good and faithful servant. Since you were trustworthy with a few things, I will put you in charge of many things. Enter into your master's joy.”
The one who had received the one talent also came forward, saying, “Master, I knew that you are a harsh man, harvesting what you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter seed.
I was afraid, so I went away and hid your talent in the ground. Look, look, here is what belongs to you.”
His master answered him, ‘You wicked and lazy servant! If you know that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter seed,
“So you should have deposited my money with the bankers, and when I came, I would have received what belongs to me with its interest.
So take the talent from him and give it to the one who has the ten talents.
For everyone who has will be given more, and he will have an abundance. But from the one who does not have, even what he has will be taken away.
And throw the useless servant out into the outer darkness. There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there.”
When the Son of Man comes in his glory, with all his angels with him, then he will sit on the throne of his glory.
All the nations will be gathered before him, and he will separate them from one another, as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats.
He will place the sheep on his right and the goats on his left.
Then the king will say to those on his right, “Come, you who are blessed by my Father, and inherit the kingdom prepared for you since the foundation of the world.
For I was hungry, and you fed me. I was thirsty, and you gave me a drink. I was a stranger, and you welcomed me.
I was naked, and you clothed me. I was sick, and you visited me. I was in prison, and you came to me.”
Then the righteous will answer him, saying, “Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you a drink?
And when did we see you as a stranger and welcome you, or naked and clothe you?
And when did we see you sick or in prison and come to you?”
The king will answer and say to them, “Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of these least brothers, you did for me.”
Then he will answer and say to the others on his left, “Depart from me, you who are cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
For I was hungry, and you did not feed me. I was thirsty, and you did not give me a drink.
I was a stranger, and you did not welcome me. I was naked, and you did not clothe me. I was sick and in prison, and you did not visit me.
Then they too will answer, saying, “Lord, when did we see you hungry or thirsty or a stranger or naked or sick or in prison and not care for you?”
Then he will answer them, saying, “Truly I tell you, insofar as you did not do it for one of these little ones, you did not do it for me.”
These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.
When Jesus had finished all these words, he said to his disciples,
“You know that in two days the Passover will take place, and the Son of Man will be handed over to be crucified.”
Then the elders and the chief priests of the people gathered in the courtyard of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas.
They plotted to seize Jesus by deceit and kill him.
But they were saying, “Not during the festival, so that there will not be an uproar among the people.”
When Jesus came to Bethany, to the house of Simon the leper,
a woman approached him with a jar of very expensive perfume. She poured it onto his head while he was reclining at the table.
When the disciples saw this, they were indignant and said, “Why was this wasted?”
“For this could have been sold for a large sum and the money given to the poor.”
When Jesus realized this, he said to them, “Why are you troubling this woman? She has done a good deed for me.”
“For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.”
“For when she poured this perfume onto my body, she did it for my burial.”
“Truly I tell you, wherever this good news is proclaimed throughout the whole world, what she has done will also be told in remembrance of her.”
Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests,
saying, “What are you willing to give me, and I will hand him over to you?” They agreed with him on thirty pieces of silver.
From that time on, he looked for an opportunity to hand him over.
On the first day of the Passover, the disciples approached Jesus, saying, “Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal for you to eat?”
He said to them, “Go into the city to a certain man and tell him, ‘The teacher says, “My time is near. I will celebrate the Passover at your house with my disciples.”’”
The disciples did as Jesus had instructed them, and they prepared the Passover meal.
When evening came, he was reclining at the table with the twelve disciples.
While they were eating, he said to them, “Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me.”
They were deeply distressed and began to say to him one by one, “Surely it is not I, Lord?”
Jesus answered, saying, “The one who dipped his hand into the bowl with me is the one who will betray me.”
The Son of Man will go as it is written about him, but woe to that man through whom the Son of Man will be betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.
Judas, who was going to betray him, answered, “Surely it is not I, Rabbi?” He said to him, “You have said it.”
While they were eating, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to his disciples, saying, “Take and eat; this is my body.”
He also took a cup, gave thanks over it, and gave it to them, saying, “Drink from it, all of you.”
“For this is my blood of the new covenant, which will be poured out for many for the forgiveness of their sins.”
“But I tell you, from now on I will not drink from the fruit of this grapevine until that day when I drink it new with you in my Father’s kingdom.”
After singing praise, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Then Jesus said to them, “You will all fall away because of me tonight, for it is written, ‘I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.’”
“But after I rise, I will go ahead of you to Galilee.”
Peter answered him, ‘Even if they all fall away because of you, I will never fall away.’
Jesus said to him, ‘Truly I tell you, tonight, before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.’
Peter said to him, “Even if I have to die with you, I will not deny you.” All the disciples were saying the same thing.
Then Jesus came with them to a field called Gethsemane. He said to the disciples, “Sit here while I go over there and pray.”
He took Peter and the two sons of Zebedee with him and began to be sorrowful and deeply troubled.
Then he said to them, “My soul is sorrowful to the point of death. Stay here and keep watch with me.”
He went a little farther, fell on his face, and prayed, saying, “My Father, if it is possible, let this cup pass me by. Yet not as I want, but as you want.”
He came to the disciples and found them sleeping. He said to Peter, “So, could you not keep watch with me for even one hour?”
“Keep watch and pray so that you do not enter into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak.”
Again he went away a second time and prayed, saying, “My Father, if this cannot pass me by unless I drink it, then let your will be done.”
Again he came and found them sleeping, for their eyes were heavy.
He left them again, went away, and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
Then he came to the disciples and said to them, “Sleep now and rest. Look, the hour has drawn near, and the Son of Man will be handed over into the hands of sinners.”
Get up; let us go. Look, the one who will betray me has come near.
While he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, arrived, and with him a crowd carrying swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and the elders of the people.
The one who betrayed him had given them a sign, saying, “The one I kiss is the man. Seize him.”
He went up to Jesus, saying, “Greetings, Rabbi!” and kissed him.
Jesus said to him, “Friend, what have you come for?” Then they came forward, laid their hands on Jesus, and seized him.
Then one of those who were with Jesus stretched out his hand, drew his sword, struck the high priest’s slave, and cut off his ear.
Then Jesus said to him, “Put your sword back into its sheath, for everyone who takes up a sword will perish by the sword.”
“Or do you not think that I can appeal to my Father, and he will put more than twelve legions of angels at my disposal right now?”
“How then will the writings of the prophets be fulfilled, which say that it must happen this way?”
At that moment Jesus said to the crowds, “Have you come out to arrest me as though I were a robber, with your swords and clubs? Every day I sat teaching in the temple, and you did not seize me.”
But all this happened so that the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled. Then all his disciples abandoned him and fled.
They seized Jesus and took him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
But Peter followed them at a distance, as far as the high priest’s courtyard. He went inside and sat with the guards to see how it would end.
The chief priests and the whole council were looking for false testimony against Jesus so that they could put him to death.
But they found none, although many false witnesses came forward. Afterward, two came forward,
saying, “This man said, ‘I can tear down this temple and build it in three days.’”
The high priest stood up and said to him, “Will you not answer? What is this testimony they are giving against you?”
But Jesus remained silent. The high priest said to him, “I put you under oath by the living God: tell us whether you are the Christ, the Son of God.”
Jesus said to him, “You have said it. Nevertheless, I tell you all: from now on you will see the Son of Man sitting at the right hand of Power and coming on the clouds of heaven.”
Then the high priest tore his clothes, saying, “He has blasphemed! We no longer need witnesses. Look, you have now heard the blasphemy!”
“What do you think?” They answered, “He deserves death.”
Then they spat in his face and punched him, while others slapped him in the face,
saying, “Prophesy for us now, Christ! Who struck you?”
Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard. A servant girl came up to him and said, “You too were with Jesus the Galilean.”
But he denied it in front of everyone, saying, “I do not know what you are talking about.”
When he went out to the gateway, another servant girl saw him and said to those there, “This man was with Jesus the Nazarene.”
Again he denied it with an oath: “I do not know the man.”
A little later, those standing there came up to Peter and said to him, “You really are one of them too, for your speech gives you away.”
Then he began to swear and curse, saying, “I do not know the man.” Immediately a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered what Jesus had said: “Before a rooster crows, you will deny me three times.” He went out and wept bitterly.
When morning came, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel together to put him to death.
They bound him, led him away, and handed him over to Pilate the governor.
Then Judas, who had betrayed him, saw that he had been condemned. He felt remorse and returned the thirty silver coins to the chief priests and the elders.
He said, “I have sinned by betraying innocent blood.” But they said, “That is not our concern. That is your responsibility.”
He threw the silver coins into the temple and left. Then he went away and hanged himself.
The chief priests took the silver coins and said, “It is not lawful to put them into the temple treasury, because they are blood money.”
After consulting together, they used the coins to buy the potter’s field as a burial place for foreigners.
For this reason, that field has been called the Field of Blood to this day.

Then what had been spoken through Jeremiah the prophet was fulfilled: “They took the thirty silver coins, the price of the one whose value had been set, whose price had been set by the people of Israel.
They gave them for the potter’s field, just as the Lord commanded us.”
Jesus stood before the governor, and the governor asked him, “Are you the king of the Jews?” Jesus said to him, “You say so.”
But when the chief priests and the elders accused him, he gave no answer.
Then Pilate said to him, “Do you not hear how much they are testifying against you?”
But he did not answer him a single word, so that the governor was greatly amazed.
At each festival, the governor customarily released one prisoner to the crowd, whichever one they wanted.
At that time they had a notorious prisoner called Barabbas.
When they had gathered, Pilate said to them, “Whom do you want me to release to you: Barabbas, or Jesus who is called the Christ?”
For he knew that they had handed him over out of envy.
While he was sitting on the judgment seat, his wife sent him a message: “Have nothing to do with this righteous man, for I have suffered greatly today in a dream because of him.”
But the chief priests and the elders persuaded the crowd to ask for Barabbas and to have Jesus killed.
The governor asked them, “Which of these two do you want me to release to you?” They said, “Barabbas.”
Pilate said, “Then what should I do with Jesus who is called the Christ?” They all said, “Crucify him!”
But he said, “Why? What evil has he done?” But they shouted all the more, “Crucify him!”

When Pilate saw that he was accomplishing nothing, but that instead the disturbance was growing worse, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd, saying, “I am innocent of this man’s blood. That is your responsibility.”
All the people answered, “His blood be on us and on our children!”
Then he released Barabbas to them. But he had Jesus flogged and handed him over to be crucified.
Then the governor’s soldiers took Jesus into the governor’s headquarters and gathered the whole company of soldiers around him.
They stripped him naked and put a scarlet cloak on him.
They wove a crown of thorns and placed it on his head, and put a reed in his right hand. They knelt before him and mocked him, saying, “Hail, king of the Jews!”
They spat in his face, took the reed, and struck him on the head.
After they had mocked him, they stripped him of the cloak, put his own clothes on him, and led him out to crucify him.
As they were going out, they found a man from Cyrene named Simon. They forced him to carry his cross.
When they came to a place called Golgotha, which is the Place of the Skull,
They gave him wine mixed with gall to drink, but when he tasted it, he did not want to drink it.
after they crucified him, they divided his clothes among themselves, casting lots for them.
And they sat there keeping watch over him.
They placed the charge against him in writing above his head: “This is the King of the Jews.”
Then two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right and one on his left.
Those passing by insulted him, shaking their heads
and saying, “You who destroy the temple and rebuild it in three days, save yourself! If you are the Son of God, come down from the cross!”
Likewise, the chief priests, along with the scribes and elders, mocked him, saying,
“He saved others, but he cannot save himself. He is the King of Israel! Let him come down from the cross now, and we will believe in him.
If he trusted in God, [?] let God rescue him now if he wants him, for he said, ‘I am the Son of God.’”
The robbers who were crucified with him also said the same thing, taunting him.
From the sixth hour of the day, darkness came over the whole land until the ninth hour.
At the ninth hour, Jesus cried out in a loud voice, saying, “Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani,” which means, “My God, my God, why have you abandoned me?”
When some of those standing there heard it, they said, ‘This man is calling for Elijah.’
Immediately one of them ran, took a sponge, filled it with sour wine, tied it to a reed, and gave him a drink.
But the others said, “Wait! Let us see whether Elijah is coming to rescue him.”
Jesus cried out in a loud voice and gave up his spirit.
And look! The curtain of the temple tore in two from top to bottom. The earth shook, and the rocks split.
The tombs opened, and many bodies of the holy people who had fallen asleep were raised.
They came out of the tombs, and after they had risen, they went into the holy city and appeared to many people.
When the centurion and those with him who were guarding Jesus saw the earthquake and what had happened, they were very afraid and said, “Truly, this was the Son of God!”
Many women were there, watching from a distance. They had followed Jesus from Galilee and served him.
Among them were Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of Zebedee’s sons.
When evening came, a rich man from Arimathea named Joseph arrived. He too had become a disciple of Jesus.
He went to Pilate and asked for Jesus’ body. Then Pilate ordered that it be given to him.
Joseph took the body and wrapped it in a clean linen cloth.
He placed it in his own new tomb, which he had cut into the rock. He rolled a large stone against the entrance of the tomb and went away.
Mary Magdalene and the other Mary were there, sitting opposite the tomb.
The next day, the day after the Preparation, the chief priests and the elders gathered before Pilate.
They said, “Sir, we remember that while he was still alive, that deceiver said, ‘After three days I will rise.’

“So order us to secure the tomb until the third day, so that his disciples do not come, steal him, and tell the people, ‘He has risen from the dead.’ Then the last deception will be worse than the first.”
Pilate said to them, “Take the guard, go, and secure it as best you know how.”
They went and secured the tomb with the guard, sealing the stone.
Late on the Sabbath, as dawn approached on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary came to see the tomb.
And look, a great earthquake occurred! For the angel of the Lord came down from heaven, approached, rolled away the stone, and sat on it.
His appearance was like lightning, and his clothing was white as snow.
The guards trembled in fear of him and became like dead people.
The angel answered the women, “Do not be afraid. I know that you are looking for Jesus, who was crucified.
“He is not here, for he has risen, just as he said. Come and see the place where he was.”
And go quickly and tell his disciples, ‘He has risen from the dead, and look, he will go ahead of you to Galilee. You will see him there.’ Look, I have told you.
They quickly left the tomb and ran with fear and great joy to tell his disciples.
And look, Jesus met them, saying, “Greetings!” They approached, took hold of his feet, and worshiped him.
Jesus said to them, “Do not be afraid. Go and tell my brothers to go to Galilee, for they will see me there.”
While they were going, some of the guard went into the city and told the chief priests everything that had happened.
They gathered the elders, took counsel, and gave the soldiers a large sum of money,
saying, “Say, ‘His disciples came during the night and stole him while we were asleep.’
“If the governor hears about this, we will persuade him and keep you free from worry.”
They took the money and did as they had been instructed. This story has spread among the Jews to this day.
The eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain Jesus had appointed for them.
When they saw him, they worshiped him, but some doubted.
Jesus came to them and spoke to them, saying, “All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me.
So go and teach all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,
teaching them to keep everything I have commanded you. And look, I am with you every day until the end of the age.”
